title: BJP Replaces Social Media Chief Amit Malviya With Deepak Mhaskey in Major Reshuffle
excerpt: India's ruling party overhauled its digital strategy team on Monday, weeks after youth-led protests amplified through social media forced the resignation of the education minister.
body:
• BJP replaced Amit Malviya, who held the social media head role since 2015, with Deepak Mhaskey as part of the first organizational reshuffle under new party president Nitin Nabin.
  • The change comes weeks after the Cockroach Janta Party, a satirical social media movement, amassed 15 million followers and helped force the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
  • Mhaskey previously served as a BJP spokesperson and IT cell head in central India, according to his LinkedIn profile.
  • The reshuffle is seen as part of the BJP's effort to retain young voters after Gen Z-led protests exposed weaknesses in the party's digital dominance.

India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party replaced its longtime social media chief Amit Malviya on Monday as part of a broader organizational reshuffle, the party said, in a move that comes weeks after youth-led protests amplified through social media forced the resignation of the country's education minister.

Malviya, who had headed the BJP's digital operations since 2015, was replaced by Deepak Mhaskey, according to a party statement reported by Reuters. The reshuffle is the first under new BJP president Nitin Nabin, who took charge in January and, at 45, is the youngest party chief in BJP history.

A Generational Challenge

The timing of the change is significant. In recent months, the BJP has faced an unprecedented digital challenge from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical social media movement born in May 2026 that went viral within days. The CJP amassed 15 million followers in less than a week — compared with fewer than 9 million for the BJP's official accounts.

https://x.com/livemint/status/2089325584577188335

The movement spearheaded largely Gen Z protests in New Delhi and other cities demanding the resignation of then-education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over leaked question papers for a national medical college entrance examination. Pradhan resigned on July 25.

Social media became a primary rallying point for the protesters, who used platforms long harnessed by the BJP to mock Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his government through raps, songs, and viral videos, according to Reuters.

"I am confident that under their leadership, the BJP's digital communication will achieve newer milestones and continue to shape India's public discourse with conviction, creativity and clarity."

— Amit Malviya, outgoing BJP social media head, on X

New Face, Uncertain Mandate

The BJP provided few details about Mhaskey's background. His LinkedIn profile identifies him as a former party spokesperson and head of the BJP's information technology cell in central India, but includes no further details about his role, according to Reuters.

Nabin did not specify the reason for the change or outline how the team would operate differently under Mhaskey's leadership. Referring to the broader reshuffle, the party president said it would further strengthen the organization and give it "new momentum."

The BJP's IT cell, formally known as the Bharatiya Janata Party Information Technology Cell, has been a cornerstone of the party's electoral strategy. Under Malviya's leadership, the operation grew to encompass an extensive digital network of roughly 150,000 social media workers who disseminate content across WhatsApp groups and other platforms, according to a report by The Washington Post.

Youth Protests Expose Digital Vulnerability

The reshuffle signals an acknowledgment within the BJP that its once-dominant digital infrastructure may need retooling to connect with younger voters. The CJP, which describes itself as representing "the lazy, the unemployed, and the chronically correct," tapped into frustrations among young Indians who make up more than half of the country's 1.42 billion population.

India's unemployment rate stood at 3.1% in 2025 for people aged 15 and above, but nearly 10% among those aged 15 to 29, rising to 13.6% in urban areas, according to government data reported by Reuters.

Nabin himself had previously taken a combative stance against the movement, calling the CJP and similar groups "virus and cockroach parties" that "can hollow out the country" and describing their members as "part of an anti-India gang."

Broader Reshuffle Underway

The social media leadership change is part of a wider organizational overhaul under Nabin, who succeeded J.P. Nadda as party president. In recent months, the BJP has appointed new state unit presidents in Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, and Tripura as it prepares for assembly elections next year in several key states.

The party's organizational retooling comes as the BJP seeks to consolidate power across India while contending with a younger, digitally savvy opposition that has proven capable of outpacing the party's own social media machinery.
